clauses.text: Confidentiality obligations shall survive for a period of three (3) years from the date of disclosure.
The obligations set forth in this Section shall survive for a period of five (5) years.
Confidentiality obligations shall survive the termination of this Agreement indefinitely and continue in perpetuity.
The receiving party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, officers, legal counsel, and financial advisors on a need-to-know basis.
Disclosure required by law, regulation, or court order shall be permitted provided the receiving party gives prompt notice to the disclosing party.
The receiving party shall not disclose any Confidential Information to any third party including professional advisors without prior written consent.
The non-solicitation obligation shall expire upon termination of this Agreement and applies only to employees directly involved in the discussions.
This Agreement may be terminated by either party upon thirty (30) days' written notice. The initial term shall be two (2) years, renewable by mutual agreement.
Each party shall, upon the other's request, return or destroy all Confidential Information and certify in writing within thirty (30) days.
The receiving party may retain one copy of the Confidential Information for legal archival purposes. Electronic copies residing in standard backup systems need not be deleted.
This Agreement constitutes the entire understanding between the parties and may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both parties.
The Disclosing Party may assign this Agreement without the Receiving Party's consent, and the Receiving Party waives any right to injunctive relief.
